sections.html:
Buchanan County is in northeast Iowa, and Independence is both the county seat and its largest city, with 6,064 residents in 2020. The county as a whole had 20,565 people that year, and about 67 percent live in rural areas. That rural share means many parcels are acreage or farm sites rather than town lots, and the tax bill follows the parcel.

Jesup (2,508) and Fairbank (1,111) are the next largest places, and both straddle a county line: Jesup is partly in Black Hawk County and Fairbank is partly in Fayette County. A Jesup house on the Black Hawk side would be taxed by that county, so pull the parcel record and confirm the county before you look for a bill.

The county assessor values property, and the county treasurer bills and collects. Both offices are in the courthouse at 210 5th Avenue NE, Independence, IA 50644.

Buchanan County property tax offices
OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerCollects tax, runs the tax sale, takes redemptions319-334-4340 (tax)
AssessorAssesses property, signs up homestead, veteran and family farm credits210 5th Ave NE

Treasurer hours for property tax are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office closes at noon on June 30 and December 31 for balancing. Online payment by card or eCheck is at pay.iowataxandtags.org.

Buchanan County taxes come due in two halves: the first on September 1 and the second on March 1. Each half is delinquent after the end of its month, September 30 and March 31. You can pay in full or in halves.

Statements are mailed in August. If a deadline lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day. Unpaid first-half taxes become delinquent in October and unpaid second-half taxes in April, with interest of 1.5 percent per month, rounded to the nearest dollar, with a $1 minimum.

  • August: tax statements mailed.
  • September 1 to 30: first half payable without penalty.
  • March 1 to 31: second half payable without penalty.
  • Third Monday in June: annual county tax sale.

Owners can protest an assessment to the county board of review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. Iowa Code section 441.37 limits a protest to five grounds: the value is not equitable with like property, the property is assessed above the legal value, it is exempt or misclassified, there is an error, or there is fraud.

The board must send back a written decision with reasons. If that answer leaves you unsatisfied, you can go on to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court. Ask the assessor which year the next reassessment falls in and whether informal reviews open earlier in April.

The assessor's office also signs people up for the homestead, veteran and family farm credit programs, which can lower a bill before you ever need an appeal.

Delinquent parcels are offered at the county tax sale, held each June by open bidding, and the third Monday in June is the standard date. A buyer pays the delinquent tax, and an owner who wants to redeem pays that amount plus 2 percent per month.

Redemption cannot be paid through the website, so call the treasurer at 319-334-4340. If redemption is not completed in time, the buyer may start steps toward a tax deed. A delinquent bill on a house you plan to sell is worth settling first, because a sold certificate adds interest and fees to your payoff.

Iowa charges a real estate transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above $500, and the seller is liable for it. The tax is paid to the county recorder, and a declaration of value must be filed when the deed is presented, or the recorder will refuse to record it.

Iowa Code section 428A.2 lists exemptions, including gifts between spouses or between parent and child, transfers to heirs without consideration and tax deeds. A sale to a buyer at full price is taxable. Of each month's receipts, 82.75 percent go to the Department of Revenue and the rest stays in the county general fund.

Sellers in Buchanan County often own a house in a small town or on rural ground, and the buyer pool is narrower than in a city. Inherited homes and houses with deferred repairs are common reasons owners look at a quick sale.

  • Pull the parcel record and confirm the county, since Jesup and Fairbank straddle county lines.
  • Ask the treasurer for the current balance on both halves.
  • Check whether a homestead, veteran or family farm credit is on file with the assessor.
  • Bring the deed so a declaration of value can be filed at recording.

When a house needs work or taxes are behind, a cash sale as-is can move faster than a listing, since there are no repair requests from a lender's appraiser or a buyer's inspector to work through.

Order of events is simple. Call the treasurer a few days before closing and ask for the balance on each half, including any interest. The title company then pays what is owed out of your proceeds. The deed goes to the recorder along with the declaration of value, and the transfer tax is collected at that point. If you hold a homestead, veteran or family farm credit, tell the assessor about the sale so the credit is not left on a house you no longer own. Keep the settlement statement with your tax papers, since it shows how the current year's bill was divided between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Buchanan County, Iowa?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Each half is delinquent after September 30 and March 31, and late interest is 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Buchanan County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the treasurer's office on the first floor of the courthouse, 210 5th Avenue NE, Independence, or online at pay.iowataxandtags.org. The tax phone is 319-334-4340.

faqs.q: When is the Buchanan County tax sale?
faqs.a: The annual sale is held in June, normally on the third Monday, though the treasurer may set another date.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Buchanan County assessment?
faqs.a: File a protest with the board of review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year, on one of the grounds in Iowa Code section 441.37.

faqs.q: Does Iowa charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The rate is 80 cents per $500 of value above $500, the seller is liable, and the county recorder collects it with a declaration of value.
